paras: The lynching of Robert Robinson was the killing of Robinson, a Black man living at 514 West 54th Place on Chicago's South Side, by a mob of white men around midnight on Saturday, June 21, 1919. The same mob shot and stabbed Ollie Harris, who was reported dying, and part of it was said to have beaten a former soldier, Charles Mitchell. Black papers in several states reported the attack as a "race war" started by whites.

According to the Associated Negro Press (ANP), a race war had been "threatening for weeks" on the South Side, and the Rev. L. K. Williams of Olivet Baptist Church spoke of a series of race riots there over several months. The Chicago Defender wrote that three weeks earlier men and boys of the same gang had marched through a nearby street, breaking windows and taking a boy's bicycle.

Word had spread that "a big fight" would come that night in Washington Park, where 200 park police kept watch. At 12:30 a.m. the Stock Yards police station was told by telephone that a white mob was "out to kill all the blacks," but the squad sent out did not find it. In the ANP's account, Robinson was "simply walking to his home" when the mob shot him several times, stabbed him in the back and beat him with billiard cues at 55th Street and Princeton Avenue. The same mob shot Ollis Harris of 5647 Grove Avenue through the stomach and stabbed him at 57th Street and Lafayette Avenue.

The Chicago Whip told it differently: more than 500 whites attacked Harris at 50th and Princeton, and Robinson, running to the scene, pleaded for him until the mob turned and shot him. When he kept fighting, the Whip said, the mob drew knives and razors, and Robinson "fell and bled to death." The Defender placed the killing near Garfield Avenue and reported that part of the mob then beat Charles Mitchell, 27, a former member of Company D, under a viaduct west of State Street.

Police Lieutenant Fred Guerney arrested about two score suspects and held eleven, withholding their names because "the Negroes might obtain vengeance"; the Baltimore Afro-American gave 48 arrests. First Deputy of Police Alcock promised, "There will be no discrimination." The Defender reported on July 12 that a coroner's inquest had been continued to July 19 at Captain Cain's recommendation; no report of its verdict, of charges, or of Harris's fate appears in the coverage. Robinson left a wife, Cecelia, and children.
Williams told Baptist ministers that "Segregation will not answer," and Julius Rosenwald likewise called segregation "out of the question."

The ANP story ran in the Omaha Monitor on June 26, the St. Louis Argus on June 27, the Cleveland Advocate, Kansas City Sun and Phoenix Tribune on June 28, and the Metropolis Weekly Gazette on July 4. Headlines blamed whites: "Whites Start a Race Riot in Chicago" in the Argus and "White Army Masses Against Blacks In War" in the Sun, while the Advocate's "Two Colored Men Dead" outran its own text. The wire called the attackers "a gang of savage hoodlums" and stressed there had been no fight, and its continuation said Black leaders blamed both rough migrants from the South and "tough whites" encouraged by the "sensational daily newspapers."

In Chicago, the Whip cast Robinson as a hero who pleaded "in the name of DEMOCRACY" and headlined Alcock's promised investigation. The Defender, under "Robinson Murdered," named the gang "Ragan's Colts" and said the mob was "permitted to operate in most any locality they see fit." Under "Policemen Asleep" it printed a white resident's claim that the mob were sons and relatives of Stock Yards policemen. By contrast, the Afro-American headed its garbled version "White Mob in Chicago Dispersed by Policemen."

The Whip dated the attack "Sunday, June 23," the ANP "shortly after Saturday midnight," and the Defender "Saturday night, June 21." The Whip put it at 50th and Princeton, the ANP at 55th and Princeton, and the Defender, correcting earlier reports, at Princeton Avenue and Garfield Boulevard. Police put the mob at 150 against the Whip's "over 500," and the Defender named the victim "Joseph Robinson, age 47."

reader.title: Lynching of Robert Robinson
bases: A white mob numbered at 150 or more, said to have set out to 'clean out the blacks', shot, stabbed and beat Robert Robinson to death and wounded at least one other Black man (A1, A5, A9); the papers also called it a 'race riot' (A5, A10).

Robinson was killed by a mob of white men, 150 by police count and over 500 by the Whip, acting with no authority (A1, A3, A5); the stated aim of the mob was racial, to kill or 'clean out' the blacks, not any accusation against him (A3, A5).

The Chicago Whip, the Associated Negro Press wire and the Chicago Defender's own reporting agree that a white mob killed Robinson and wounded Harris, though they differ on place and sequence (A1, A5, A9, A16).

framing.detail: St. Louis Argus ran the ANP wire as 'Whites Start a Race Riot in Chicago', calling the attackers 'a gang of savage hoodlums' and stressing there had been no fight.
Chicago Whip cast Robinson as a hero who pleaded 'in the name of DEMOCRACY' and headlined Alcock's promised 'rigid investigation'.
Chicago Defender headlined 'Robinson Murdered' and 'Policemen Asleep', named Ragan's Colts and said the mob operated without hindrance.
Baltimore Afro-American's short version was headed 'White Mob in Chicago Dispersed by Policemen'.
Cleveland Advocate, Kansas City Sun, Phoenix Tribune and Metropolis Weekly Gazette reprinted the ANP wire; the Sun headlined 'White Army Masses Against Blacks In War'.
